text:
Matching 99 training negatives provides only partial alignment: eligibility rules, sampling distribution, loss, and user weighting also determine the objective. Exclude padding and the positive target; excluding observed training positives reduces contradictory supervision, but must not consult hidden held-out interactions. Unobserved items can still be false negatives; sequential-recommendation research documents this problem ([UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116)). Sampling without replacement matches candidate uniqueness and avoids duplicate negatives receiving repeated weight. For uniformly sampled pairwise losses, replacement preserves the expected average loss but changes variance; for candidate-softmax losses, duplicates also change competition in the denominator. Thus, 99-negative cross-entropy remains a surrogate for HR@10, not its equivalent.

Weighting implications follow directly from loss aggregation: sampling interactions uniformly favors active users; sampling users uniformly and averaging each user’s valid-position losses gives users equal total weight. Uniform user sampling followed by a global token-average loss still favors longer histories. Equal category weighting aligns with macro-average evaluation. Training on all historical positions also differs from evaluating one final held-out target per user; matching negative count does not remove that context mismatch.

Sampled gains alone cannot establish full-catalog improvement. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show that sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons even in expectation. Mathematically, with M eligible negatives and R outranking the target, sampled HR@10 succeeds when a hypergeometric draw of 99 contains at most nine of those R items—different from requiring R≤9 across the catalog. Evidence for catalog gains requires full-catalog validation under identical exclusions; additional candidate samples measure robustness but cannot prove equivalence. Under the pinned protocol, report improvements specifically as sampled-candidate validation gains.
